question_text: What is the recommended speed that applies to cars and motorcycles on autobahns?
comment: On motorways cars and motorcycles have to keep an advisory speed limit of 130 km/h. In addition, driving on a freeway is only permitted to vehicles exceeding 60 km/h.

question_text: You are driving in the left of two lanes and approaching a vehicle that has just started to overtake. What do you do?

options.text: Keep an adequate distance behind the vehicle in front
Allow the vehicle in front to overtake
Close up to the vehicle in front, sound your horn and flash your lights

correct_answers.text: Keep an adequate distance behind the vehicle in front
Allow the vehicle in front to overtake

comment: You allow this vehicle to overtake by maintaining a safety distance. As the vehicle changes from the right, be prepared that its speed is lower than yours despite acceleration. Slow your pace down, if necessary. Never tailgate, honk or flash.

question_text: You are driving on the autobahn in light traffic. How long are you allowed to stay in the left-hand lane?

options.text: As long as is necessary to overtake other vehicles
As long as you are driving behind a vehicle which is overtaking in the left-hand lane
All the time, provided no other vehicle wants to overtake you

correct_answers.text: As long as is necessary to overtake other vehicles
As long as you are driving behind a vehicle which is overtaking in the left-hand lane

comment: The left lane may generally only be used for the purpose of overtaking. If the preceding vehicle overtakes, it can be assumed that the following car driver will also overtake. Therefore, it is allowed here to use the left lane. In all other cases, you have to drive on the right.

question_text: What applies on clearways for motor vehicles only?

options.text: No U-turns
Join the clearway only at crossroads and junctions
In darkness, you may drive faster than the range of visibility allowed by dipped headlights

correct_answers.text: No U-turns
Join the clearway only at crossroads and junctions

comment: You may only enter at intersections or T-junctions on motorways. Turning on motorways is prohibited. The regulations regarding speed differ from those that apply on the freeway. On highways you must not drive faster than the range of the low beam allows.

question_text: What top speed must be entered in the vehicle documents to allow the vehicle's use on autobahns?
comment: A highway or freeway was built for high-speed traffic. That's why only vehicles that can reach a speed of more than 60 km/h are allowed to drive here. If you’re not entirely sure if own vehicle can drive that fast, it is noted in the car documents.

question_text: A traffic jam has formed on a three-lane autobahn. Where must the channel for emergency vehicles be formed?

options.text: Between the left-hand and the middle lanes
Between the middle and right-hand lanes
On the hard shoulder

correct_answers.text: Between the left-hand and the middle lanes

comment: When traffic stops on freeways or on roads outside of built-up areas with at least two lanes in one direction, vehicles must form a free lane for the passage of police and support vehicles. If a road has three lanes into one direction, then the middle is considered to be between the left and the middle lane.

question_text: You are driving in a merging lane. What should you do?

options.text: Drive past to the right of slower-moving vehicles driving on the through-lane and merge in before them
Accelerate appropriately, do not pull up if possible, merge while observing the right of way
Always drive to the end of the merging lane, pull up there and then enter lane

correct_answers.text: Drive past to the right of slower-moving vehicles driving on the through-lane and merge in before them
Accelerate appropriately, do not pull up if possible, merge while observing the right of way

comment: On an acceleration lane it is allowed to drive faster on the right than on the continuous lane. In order to merge, you as a car driver must accelerate adequately and observe the right of way and the safety distance.

question_text: What must you do now?

options.text: - as far to the right as possible
- as far to the left as possible
- in the centre

correct_answers.text: - as far to the right as possible

comment: You approach the end of a traffic jam on the freeway. Turn on the hazard light. Form an alley in the middle of the lane for the passage of police and helping vehicles: on roads with three lanes for one direction, form an alley between the left and middle lane. Therefore, you have to drive far to the right. This rule applies outside built-up areas and on freeways.

question_text: What should you do?

options.text: I continue driving
I get in line on the hard shoulder
I stop on my lane and wait for a gap

correct_answers.text: I continue driving

comment: They want to leave the freeway. You can see that traffic is stalling in your intended exit. Since you are not allowed to drive on the hard shoulder and wait on the lane, you behave correctly if you continue driving and use the next exit in order to exit the freeway.

question_text: What must you do when a traffic jam forms on this road?

options.text: - drive as far to the left as possible
- drive as far to the right as possible
- continuing driving in the centre

correct_answers.text: - drive as far to the left as possible

comment: Any car driver must cooperate in forming an alley in the middle of the road for the passage of police and support vehicles in case of congestion on freeways and on out-of-town roads with more than one lane. Do not drive on the side strip, this is prohibited.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I warn the driver by sounding my horn and flashing my lights
I drive over to the right-side as far as possible
I notify the police

correct_answers.text: I warn the driver by sounding my horn and flashing my lights
I drive over to the right-side as far as possible
I notify the police

comment: You meet a wrong-way driver on the freeway exit. By driving as far to the right as possible, you can best counteract a collision with the wrong-way driver. Now other road users must be warned of this acute danger. For this reason, you must inform the police.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: I accelerate and merge in front of the [truck]
I slow down and merge between the [red car] and the [truck]
I slow down and merge after the [yellow vehicle]

correct_answers.text: I accelerate and merge in front of the [truck]

comment: They have already passed the truck on the acceleration lane on the right-hand side of the freeway. If you continue to accelerate, you can drive onto the main lane before the end of the lane. You should do that.

question_text: You want to exit the motorway. What is the right course of action in this situation?

options.text: I move into the left-hand lane
I watch out for oncoming vehicles
I continue by driving on the hard shoulder

correct_answers.text: I move into the left-hand lane

comment: You flash and leave the freeway at the exit. The route to the turn of the exit is used to decelerate. Drive quickly off the highway, then reduce your pace. Drive into the corner at a moderately reduced speed.

question_text: What must you do if you find yourself in a traffic jam on motorways and on highways with two lanes travelling in the same direction?

options.text: - drive as far to the right as possible in the right-hand lane
- drive as far to the left as possible in the left-hand lane
- drive as far to the left as possible in the right-hand lane

correct_answers.text: - drive as far to the right as possible in the right-hand lane
- drive as far to the left as possible in the left-hand lane

comment: If vehicles stand or drive at walking speed on freeways or on roads outside of built-up areas with at least two lanes for one direction, the following applies: You, as a car driver, must participate in forming a free lane between the leftmost and rightmost lane for the passage of police and support vehicles.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I stay in the middle lane
I move into the left-hand lane
I move into the right-hand lane

correct_answers.text: I stay in the middle lane

comment:
You must stay in the middle lane because there are vehicles in the left and right lanes that you would obstruct.
In the right lane, a motorbike is coming onto the motorway from the slip road. In the left lane is the car that just overtook you.

question_text: You want to leave the motorway at the next exit. What is the correct course of action in this situation?

options.text: I observe the traffic behind me
I turn on my right-side indicators now
I begin now to smoothly brake down to 60 km/h

correct_answers.text: I observe the traffic behind me
I turn on my right-side indicators now

comment:
When leaving the motorway, you should set the indicator at least 300 m before the exit.
Always keep a close eye on the traffic behind you when driving on the motorway. Especially when exiting the motorway, make sure that nobody tries to overtake you on the right.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I accelerate
I move into the middle lane

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed

comment: Reduce your speed and allow the blue car to join the motorway while keeping a safe distance.

question_text: What can you expect now?

options.text: - brake
- stay in the middle lane
- accelerate

correct_answers.text: - brake
- stay in the middle lane

comment:
You should expect the truck in front of you to slow down because the other truck in the right lane is already slowing down and has its hazard lights on. You also have to expect that the truck will stay in the middle lane because it doesn't have enough space to get into the right lane. 
If a dangerous situation is identified on the motorway, the hazard warning lights may be switched on in order to warn all following vehicles in good time. Dangerous situations usually include accidents, traffic jams or slow traffic.

question_text: Your vehicle has broken down on the autobahn. What must you remember when having it towed away?

options.text: You must leave the autobahn at the next exit
During towing, both vehicles must have their hazard warning lights switched on
You may continue along the autobahn to the exit nearest a suitable garage

correct_answers.text: You must leave the autobahn at the next exit
During towing, both vehicles must have their hazard warning lights switched on

comment: When towing on the freeway, the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle must have their hazard lights switched on. It's only allowed to tow on the freeway until the next exit. Then, the freeway must be left.

question_text: What applies on autobahns?

options.text: No stopping on the roadway and hard shoulder
No reversing
In darkness, under no circumstances drive faster than the range of visibility allowed by dipped headlights

correct_answers.text: No stopping on the roadway and hard shoulder
No reversing

comment: On the freeway you are only allowed to drive forward and only in one given direction. Reversing, turning and stopping is strictly prohibited on the roadway as well as on the side strip.

question_text: You are driving on the motorway and have missed the exit. What is the right course of action?

options.text: I continue driving and leave the motorway at one of the next exits
I reverse back on the hard shoulder, because the exit is less than 100 m behind me
I stop on the hard shoulder to plan my subsequent route

correct_answers.text: I continue driving and leave the motorway at one of the next exits

comment: Continue until the next exit and leave the freeway there. Now you can drive back to the missed exit on the other side of the freeway. You must not stop or drive backwards.

question_text: How can lane changing assist help you in this situation without steering override?

options.text: - warns of a possible collision with a vehicle in the middle lane
- performs a lane change independently
- brakes the speed of my vehicle

correct_answers.text: - warns of a possible collision with a vehicle in the middle lane

comment: Lane Change Assist recognises the vehicle in the middle lane as a hazard and warns you not to change to that lane. To change lanes on your own would require steering intervention. Lane Change Assist does not interfere with your speed.

question_text: What is prohibited when using motorways?

options.text: Stopping on the hard shoulder
Reversing
Performing U-turns

correct_answers.text: Stopping on the hard shoulder
Reversing
Performing U-turns

comment:
According to the StVO § 18 motorways and motor drivers:
(7) Turning and reversing are prohibited.
(8) hold, also on the side stripes, is forbidden.

question_text: Why should you have the traffic information switched on, when driving on the motorway?

options.text: - gives warnings about motorists heading in the wrong direction
- provides reports about traffic jams
- is a prescribed requirement for travelling on the motorway

correct_answers.text: - gives warnings about motorists heading in the wrong direction
- provides reports about traffic jams

comment: Drivers are not required to listen to traffic news, but traffic news are indispensable for a smooth journey. Traffic news inform about traffic jams, traffic accidents and construction sites. Warnings about wrong-way drivers have already prevented a lot of serious accidents.
